blocking_repair.root_cause: The derived illegal-transition count had an increment rule, monotonicity and append-only-ness, but no scope, no initial value and no reset point. SP-094's initial condition could not name it, because the count is a T-fact and SP-103 makes the L-fact and T-fact classes disjoint.
blocking_repair.why_it_was_a_regression: v0.2 scoped the count 'over the supplied trace' in both SP-043 and SP-102. v0.3 deleted that phrase from both while presenting the surrounding edit as a repair. v0.2 was sound on this coordinate; v0.3 was not.
blocking_repair.attack_it_permitted: On day 2 of a Durable *Daily* Ritual Ledger, a run reaches SP-094's stated initial condition (idle, empty durable history, empty pending) carrying illegal_transition_count = 1 from an earlier DaySlot, and fails the founder's sealed acceptance predicate illegal_transition_count = 0 while violating no clause.
minimum_structural_repair: SP-102 — the T-fact set is scoped to one presented sequence and begins empty for each; monotonic within it, never across.
SP-043 — the count is derived over one presented sequence and has no existence outside it: zero at the first element, incremented only by an INVALID_TRANSITION within that sequence.

SP-094 — the required vector IS a complete presented sequence, all six acceptance values are evaluated over it and no other, and a proper suffix of a longer presented sequence is expressly not the required vector however closely its L-facts resemble the stated initial condition.
blocking_repair.why_not_blocked_by_founder_or_source: The repair required no change to founder-sealed meaning, no commission amendment, and no founder decision. The scoping phrase v0.3 deleted was authored in v0.2 and is restored on authored grounds. BLOCKED_BY_FOUNDER_OR_SOURCE_DECISION is therefore NOT returned.
blocking_repair.counterexample_rerun: FT-14 presents the CR-003 day-2 trace as two presented sequences and falsifies any accumulation across them, any nonzero count in the DaySlot-2 observation, and any attempt to satisfy SP-094 by pointing at a suffix.

SP-091 reduced to the founder's sentence alone; the authored comparison rule split into SP-095. The phrase 'presented sequence' occurs 0 times across all three L1 pins, so a FOUNDER_SEALED_L1 row was being parameterized by an AUTHOR-PROPOSED clause. The SP-090/SP-094 technique applied one row down.

SP-155 makes a disposition record that misdescribes its substrate nonconforming — without it, two embodiments could conform by both misreporting. SP-096 declares the singleton required-vector domain rather than concealing it.

what_a_reviewer_should_be_told_to_attack: Whether the T-fact scoping actually closes CR3-B01 or relocates it — in particular whether any acceptance predicate can still be satisfied by a suffix, and what happens when a presented sequence legitimately spans a DaySlot boundary.

Whether the declared loss class is genuinely comparable, or merely a second undefined token: SP-151 draws it from an embodiment's published capability declaration, and nothing in the SemanticProgram constrains that vocabulary.
Whether SP-155's veridicality obligation is enforceable at all, or is prose.
Whether SP-162's content-presence choice (a supplied empty value IS present) creates any new divergence downstream.
The 21 changed and 12 added rows, individually.
Whether the rebuilt auditor's new positive checks can themselves be gamed.
requested_next_action.secondary_option: Founder adjudication of A-01…A-08 could in principle proceed in parallel, since the docket is now accurate by the candidate's own rule — but CR-003's own standard was that even a PASS means only READY_FOR_FOUNDER_ADJUDICATION, and v0.4 has no review at all.
